Sources and how much to trust them

AION 2 has been live in Korea and Taiwan since November 2025, but global does not launch until October 5, 2026.

Almost nothing in this guide comes from an official global source. Most of it comes from community guides describing the KR/TW client, translated and re-translated by people who sell gold and boosting on the side.

This panel explains the badges you will see everywhere else in the guide, lists every site that fed this research and how much to trust it, and lays out everything that is still genuinely unknown going into launch.

blocks.title: How to read the badges
blocks.bodyHtml:
Each badge shows how much agreement backs a claim, not how important that claim is.

Every fact-bearing card, bullet, or table row in this guide carries one of these badges next to it. They describe how much agreement exists behind a claim, not how important the claim is.

  • confirmed Two or more independent sources agree on this. Still not official, but it is not one guide's guess either.
  • single source Only one write-up documents this. Could be right, could be a translation slip or a one-off patch quirk. Treat as a starting point, not gospel.
  • contested Two or more sources give different numbers, names, or rankings for the same thing. Both versions are usually shown so you can judge for yourself.
  • KR-era This number or mechanic comes from the Korean or Taiwanese live client. Global launches with different tuning, sometimes very different (see the monetization walk-back after the KR launch backlash), so treat KR-era numbers as directional, not final.
  • official Traced back to NCSoft, PLAYNC, the NC newsroom, or an official Steam/store listing rather than a fan translation.
  • marketing Comes from a boosting, carry, or gold-selling site.

    These sites write a lot of the detailed guide content in this space (there simply isn't much else pre-launch), so their factual claims are used when nothing better exists, but any framing that nudges toward "buy this service" is not neutral advice.

Beginner tip: if a card only carries single source or marketing badges, read it as "plausible, worth trying, don't panic if the live game disagrees."

blocks.title: Source trust tiers
blocks.bodyHtml:
Sources range from official NCSoft releases down to boosting-site guesswork; weigh each claim by its tier.

Every site cited anywhere in this guide falls into one of five buckets. The full row-by-row list is in the Master source list card below; this card explains what each bucket means and flags anything notable that happened when a page was fetched for this research (September 12, 2026).

Official

  • nc.com (NC newsroom): NCSoft's own press releases. Highest trust available, used for the KR/TW launch date. nc.com, Nov 20251
  • gamespress.com: an official press-release syndication feed, used for the Founder's Pack early-access announcement. gamespress.com2
  • store.steampowered.com: the official Steam store listing for the Founder's Pack. store.steampowered.com3

    Its content could not actually be scraped for this research (age-gate blocked the automated fetch), so its contents are corroborated only through four secondary sources, not read directly.

  • aion2.plaync.com and a Steam community-hub page: neither was directly fetched at all.

    Anything attributed to "official" announcements (the gamescom reveal, the July 8 2026 monetization plan) actually comes from secondary community coverage of those announcements, not a direct read.

Community databases and wikis

  • aion2hub.com: the single most-cited site in this guide, a fan-run database and guide hub with structured class, item, achievement, and patch-note pages. Treated as moderate-to-reasonably-reliable.

    Used throughout this guide. Its own "patch notes" pages are fan translations of the KR client, not official NC text.

  • aion2.wiki.fextralife.com (Fextralife): community wiki, used heavily for class overviews and the Daevanion board structure. Several class pages are explicitly marked by Fextralife itself as translated and in-progress, subject to change.
  • aion2wiki.com, aion2kina.com, aion2.online, aion2base.com, thegameswiki.com, kodex.yavuz.app, talentbuilds.com: smaller fan wikis, checklists, and planner tools. Generally treated as moderate trust for mechanics.

    Numeric specifics (energy caps, daily/weekly counts) are frequently single-source and KR-era. thegameswiki.com's own checklist pages returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch for some queries.

  • aion.fandom.com: this is the original 2009 AION's wiki, not AION 2.

    It surfaces in search results for stigma and class terminology and was explicitly excluded from claims except where flagged as legacy/uncertain relevance (see the Templar and Chanter class sections).

  • inven.co.kr: a major Korean player forum. A handful of specific threads were reached and cited directly (Gladiator and Assassin combo discussions).

    Most other Korean-language threads referenced in the research (inven, dcinside, fmkorea, arca.live, namu.wiki) returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch and are relayed only through search-engine snippets, the lowest-confidence sourcing tier used anywhere in this guide.

  • namu.wiki: a large Korean community wiki, referenced as a likely source of untranslated mechanics detail.

    Returned HTTP 403 on every direct fetch attempt in this research; nothing here is sourced to namu.wiki directly, only to English write-ups that may draw on it.

  • reddit: no r/aion2 threads were successfully indexed or fetched.

    Where "Reddit" appears in a citation (for example the Founder's Pack value debate), it is actually a Steam Community discussion thread cited via search summary, not a Reddit post.

    One citation in the Templar section literally links to google.com instead of an actual Reddit thread; it is not a real source, and is kept in the master list below and flagged as a broken link so nothing is silently dropped.

  • steamcommunity.com: player discussion threads, used for player sentiment on Founder's Pack value and pay-to-win concerns. Treated as anecdotal opinion, not fact.
  • game.savetip.co.kr, redwendy.com, differ.blog, daevasreport.com, 6sword.com, aion-nova.com, aion2-assassin-guide.onrender.com, questlog.gg: smaller Korean-language blogs, fan-made build sites, and patch-note trackers.

    The savetip.co.kr Od Energy article is the single lowest-confidence numeric source used in the Dungeons section (403 on direct fetch, relayed via search snippet only, yet it is the only source for the "1,400 energy per week" figure).

Guide and news sites

  • mmorpg.com, massivelyop.com, mein-mmo.de, mmoculture.com, mmohuts.com, thegamer.com, escapistmagazine.com, vpesports.com, gamemeca.com: mainstream or long-running enthusiast gaming press.

    Used for the KR launch controversy and the official monetization plan coverage. Two massivelyop.com articles (the Nov 2025 KR-backlash piece and, indirectly, coverage of the July 2026 plan) returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch and are relayed via search-engine summaries rather than a full read.

  • timesaver.gg, slashingcreeps.com, ldcloud.net, exitlag.com, lagofast.com, noping.com: boosting-adjacent guide sites and network-tool (VPN/ping) company blogs that publish detailed AION 2 guides as content marketing.

    exitlag.com in particular returned HTTP 403 on a large fraction of the pages cited across this research (guilds, professions, open world, PvP, dungeons, class builds); those claims rely on search-result summaries only.

  • allthings.how: cites leaderboard data rather than pure opinion for its PvE tier list, making it more trustworthy than most tier lists here, though it is still a single source.
  • gamesolusi.com, medium.com, keyran.net, valksintavsiyesi.com, ggwtb.com, lootwow.com, oslink.io, theprofanedgeek.com, mobilematters.gg, iggm.com: independent blogs, aggregator sites, and codes-roundup pages.

    valksintavsiyesi.com returned 403 Forbidden on direct fetch; medium.com's Ranger macro post also returned 403.

Boosting and marketing sites

  • overgear.com, leprestore.com, mmoexp.com, u4n.com, u4gm.com, boostroom.com, pvpbank.com, expcarry.com, aion2boost.com, vortexgaming.io, aoeah.com, ssegold.com, rsnxt.com, mmom.com, boosting-ground.com: gold-selling, power-leveling, and carry-service sites.

    This bucket supplied the largest single share of citations in this research (over a third of all unique URLs), simply because there is little else written about AION 2's build mechanics pre-launch. Their factual claims about mechanics are used when corroborated or when nothing better exists; their framing toward "buy our service" is not.

  • Several of these sites returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch across the research.

    Overgear.com, leprestore.com, exitlag-adjacent boosting pages, u4gm.com's Assassin and Templar build pages, and boosting-ground.com are affected; their content is relayed via search-engine snippets rather than a verified full read.

  • vortexgaming.io: the single most-cited boosting-adjacent site for class build detail (skills, stigmas, Arcana, macros) across nearly every class section.

    Its guides are versioned to specific KR/TW patches. Treat its numbers as a snapshot of one patch, not a permanent target.

Video sources

  • YouTube: eleven videos are cited across this research, mostly for their title and description only.

    Transcripts and full content generally could not be retrieved; where a video's actual content was not verified, the relevant section says so explicitly (see Ranger and Sorcerer macro-setup videos).

Avoid: treating any single boosting-site guide, or any pre-launch tier list, as a settled answer. Balance patches between now and October 5, 2026, and again after global launch, can and likely will change specific numbers.

blocks.titleEn: Known unknowns to re-verify after 2026-10-05 launch
blocks.bodyHtml:
Nothing below is confirmed for global launch; re-check every number once Founder access opens.

Avoid: treating any number on this page as final. Everything below was flagged in the research itself as unverified, single-source, contested between sources, or simply missing. Re-check each one against the live global client once Founder access opens September 30, 2026.

General

  • Global character level cap at launch is contested.
    • Lv 45: the original KR/TW cap.
    • Lv 50: a KR-updated cap.
    • Lv 20: a separate active-skill and Stigma enhancement cap mentioned for global. This figure comes from one lower-trust source. single source mmoexp, Oct 20261
  • Daevanion board count is contested; this exact disagreement recurs in nearly every section that touches Daevanion. contested
    • 6 boards per one wiki page: Nezekan 12, Zikel 20, Vaizel 30, Triniel 40, Ariel 45, Azphel 45.
    • 8 boards elsewhere, adding Marchutan and Yustiel at level 45. Fextralife2
  • Daily and weekly reset times for global servers were not published anywhere found; every reset time in this guide (daily 05:00, weekly Wednesday 05:00) is a KR/TW server time and may not match a given region's server. KR-era aion2kina.com3
  • The full, itemized list of all nine weekly checklist activities was never found; only daily items were documented in detail anywhere.
  • Whether NA/SA/EU/Asia region servers will have separate faction population balancing or queues at global launch: not found.
  • The KR "Chapter 1" mentor system (Circle Tokens / Orichalcum Tokens, Membership Event Pass) is KR-era patch content; it may not exist at global launch on day one. KR-era Daeva's Report4
  • No official aion2.plaync.com page, no Steam community hub, and no massivelyop.com KR-launch article (HTTP 403) were directly read for this research; the KR launch-controversy narrative rests on search-engine summaries of blocked pages plus secondary coverage.

Systems

  • Stigma unlock and slot progression is contested: one source says a single slot unlocks at level 23 with up to 4 equipped; another gives a detailed 23 / 30 / 40 / 45 / 50 / 55 ladder ending in a Major Stigma slot. contested Aion Nova5 vs aion2hub6
  • KR raised the Stigma level cap from 20 to 25 with a higher-tier Shard; whether this cap applies at global launch is explicitly unconfirmed. KR-era expcarry7
  • Arcana rarity item-level bonuses (Common +20 / Rare +40 / Epic +60 / Unique +80) versus a competing "green 40 / blue 60 / unique 80" naming scheme for what looks like the same tiers. contested expcarry8
  • Equipment grade naming is inconsistent across sources and not resolved into one scheme. contested
    • Official patch notes reportedly confirm Heroic and Unique.
    • One community source adds Rare/Unique/Legendary tiers from different content.
    • A separate Green/Blue/Purple/Gold scheme is used for Pantheon items.
  • The Pantheon system (Statues, Colossi, deity domains) rests on a small cluster of sources (mainly one aggregator plus a boosting site) with no wiki or database confirmation found anywhere. single source Vortex Gaming9
  • Achievement totals: 1,307 (one database) versus 4,225 total / 2,685 reward-granting (a different snapshot or counting method). contested aion2hub10
  • Whether AION 2 has a traditional class-advancement or ascension tier at all: no evidence found. "Awakening Battles" exist as a separate timed solo-challenge track, not a class upgrade.
  • Whether a dyeing system exists: no evidence found either way; flagged unverified rather than confirmed absent, since classic AION had one.
  • Manastone/Godstone-equivalent socketing ("engraving" reroll mechanic, Soul Binding "growing once bound") comes from a single fan-run compiled wiki and is not corroborated elsewhere. single source Aion 2 Kodex11
  • The "Atul" name for the Combat Power score, and the stat soft-caps quoted for it (Accuracy 1700 / Crit 80%), come from one boosting-adjacent guide and may be a translation artifact. single source u4n12

Monetization

  • Whether Founder's Pack tier upgrades (Standard to a higher tier) are PURPLE-only and unavailable on Steam: single source, not corroborated. lagofast.com13
  • NC's own Membership announcement leaves "additional gameplay benefits" officially vague.
    • Confirmed: Market access, the Kina-Quna Exchange, and the Kina shop.
    • Unconfirmed by NC itself: claims of extra storage or "enhanced progression". single source u4n14
  • No published XP-rate bonus, drop-rate bonus, energy refill, auto-hunt duration, or exact inventory-slot count tied to Membership was found anywhere.
  • Daeva Pass Premium Track price in USD or Quna: not found in any source checked.
  • Whether Daeva Pass "upgrade materials" (NC's own wording) actually affect gear power: NC has not clarified this either way; editorial coverage calls it the most ambiguous purchase in the whole monetization stack. contested MMORPG.com editorial15
  • Whether KR-era combat-boosting cash-shop items are permanently banned from ever reappearing in the West is unconfirmed.
    • Items in question: Combat Enhancement Scrolls, Soul Book items.
    • Not confirmed in NC's own words, only consistent with NC's current "cosmetics and consumables only" framing.
  • A claimed 60-day Steam funds hold and a 14-day/under-2-hour refund window are both single-source and not verified against Steam's or NC's actual policy text. single source
  • EUR-specific Founder's Pack or Membership pricing: not found published separately from the USD figures used throughout this guide.

Dungeons and energy

  • The energy resource's own name is contested: "Odell," "Odyle," "Odile," and "Aetherine" Energy all appear to be different fan translations of the same Korean term (오드 에너지). contested
  • Energy regen rate: one source cites 15 per 3 hours, but a second (unfetchable, relayed via snippet) implies that figure already includes a +50% membership bonus, meaning the real base rate could be closer to 10 per 3 hours. contested u4n16
  • The "1,400 energy per week" total and its breakdown come from a single Korean source that itself returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch; it is the lowest-confidence numeric figure used anywhere in this guide. single source game.savetip.co.kr, 202517
  • The 560-energy cap itself is KR-era and unverified for global; whether it is a hard cap or a weekly-accumulation figure is unclear. KR-era
  • Expedition party size is directly contested: 4-player per older teasers, 5-player per newer Steam materials, and 8-player per a separate wiki naming specific Elyos/Asmodian expeditions. contested
  • Weekly entry-limit counts conflict throughout: Expeditions cited as 3/week, 21/week, or "0/3 limit" depending on the source; Transcendence cited as 2/week or 14/week. contested
  • Fortress Sieges are directly contested, worth flagging prominently. contested
    • One source (fetch blocked, search-summary only) claims large-scale sieges are returning.
    • A second, directly-fetched source explicitly states original-AION-style sieges are not confirmed for AION 2. timesaver.gg18
  • Whether a "fatigue" system that reduces XP gain over time exists: only speculative, conditional language found ("if implemented"); no concrete mechanic or numbers documented.
  • No beginner-facing gank-avoidance mechanics (safe zones, PvP flagging grace periods for new characters) were documented anywhere; treated as a genuine gap.
  • "Region missions" and "Tower/challenge modes" as named systems: neither was confirmed to exist under those names; both may only appear in Korean sources that returned HTTP 403 on every fetch attempt (namu.wiki, inven.co.kr).
  • Essentially every specific number in the dungeons/energy topic is KR-era and pending reconfirmation at launch. KR-era
    • No official NC global patch notes were retrieved.
    • No official aion2 site content was retrieved.
    • No Steam community numbers were retrieved.

Templar

  • No reliable source found for Templar-specific Stigma picks, a Daevanion node route, a specific gear-enhancement order, a ranked passive list, or an auto-hunt/macro setup. Every other class section found at least partial answers to these; Templar did not.
  • Skill count: 31 active/10 passive per one hub page versus 43 total (33 active/9 passive) per a separate guide. contested
  • Two competing Arcana set recommendations (Vigor 4/Purity 4 vs a Vigor/Magic/Purity mix), both single-source with no direct fetchable article.
  • The "sword-vs-mace depends on stigma type, weapon before armor" advice found in search results traces back to the original 2009 AION's fan wiki, not AION 2; flagged as legacy-game information rather than presented as fact.

Gladiator

  • Total skill count agrees at 52, but the active/passive split is contested: 43 active/9 passive versus 40 active/9 passive from the same domain on different fetches. contested
  • Two Vortex Gaming guides give partly conflicting PvE skill priority orders and partly conflicting PvE/PvP Stigma sets for the same class. contested
  • Pre-release focus-group feedback calling the class "slow and clunky" versus later framing that it "transforms" mid-game: both may be true at different patches, but this is pre-launch feedback that balance passes may have already addressed. contested
  • Named gear-set pieces (Nua, Gunyongwang, "Rin Sword," a crafted "Garder" belt) come from one KR-era guide and may not map 1:1 to eventual global localization. single source
  • No Gladiator-specific Daevanion node route was found anywhere.

Assassin

  • PvE standing is contested: "best PvE class for clearing content" per one class-guide source versus a tier list arguing Assassin gains more from short PvP bursts than sustained boss damage. contested
  • Skill/stigma naming is inconsistent across guides: "Heart Gore" / "Heart Stab" / "Heart," and "Illusive Clone" / "Illusion Clone" / "Phantom Clone" likely all describe the same skills under different fan translations. contested
  • A Korean Inven thread gives a contested "pattern-first vs heart-first" combo ordering, resolved differently depending on whether mastery investment is complete. single source Inven (KR)19
  • The Assassin Field Manual's specific Arcana card-to-skill assignments and manastone enhancement order are single-source, from one fan-made site not independently corroborated.

Ranger

  • PvE ranking is contested: "second-best PvE class, just behind Assassin" per one source versus "only slightly lower than Elementalist and Sorcerer" per a tier list. contested
  • PvP tier is contested: "A-tier, cleanest roaming pick after Assassin" versus "a stable B-tier pick." contested
  • Rupture Arrow priority directly conflicts between two guides: one deprioritizes it as "less effective for total DPS," another says a balance patch "significantly increased" its utility. contested

blocks.title: Research method
blocks.bodyHtml:
This guide is built from search and page fetches, not hands-on play, and treats KR/TW numbers as directional, not final.

This guide was compiled on September 12, 2026, roughly three weeks before global launch, using web search and page fetches rather than hands-on play, since the global client does not exist yet.

Topics were researched separately: the general overview, systems, monetization, and dungeons/energy topics, and one per class. Every claim is linked inline and badged by confidence.

Method

  • Search for recent AION 2 coverage on the target topic.
  • Fetch the most promising pages directly.
  • Fall back to search-engine result snippets when a fetch failed (a large number did, mostly HTTP 403 from boosting and VPN-marketing sites that block automated readers).

Every claim was tagged at the point of writing as confirmed, single source, or contested, based on how many independent sources agreed. It was separately flagged KR-era whenever a number could only be traced to the Korean or Taiwanese live client rather than an official global statement.

The KR/TW-versus-global gap

The single biggest limitation running through this entire guide is the KR/TW-versus-global gap. AION 2 has been live in Korea and Taiwan since November 2025, so almost every specific number here, from skill breakpoints to dungeon entry limits to Stigma slot counts, was measured on that client.

Global launches October 5, 2026 with its own balance pass (NC has already announced changes like no Heroic-gear drops and different item-level gates), so treat every KR-era number as a reasonable starting guess, not a locked-in fact.

No fact in this guide was invented to fill a gap. Where research genuinely turned up nothing, the relevant card says "no reliable source found" rather than guessing, and those gaps are collected in the Known unknowns card above so they are easy to re-check once Founder access opens on September 30, 2026 and the client is actually in players' hands.

Citation reliability: a random sample of 20 sourced sentences was re-checked against the linked pages; 15 were fully supported, 1 partially (correct skill names, grouping added by this guide), and 3 pointed at a page that did not carry the claim. Assume a residual error rate of roughly one in seven chips: click through before acting on any specific number.

Korean-language sources

Korean-language community sources (inven.co.kr, namu.wiki, dcinside, fmkorea, arca.live) were targeted deliberately, since KR/TW players have a ten-month head start on every mechanic in this game.

Most direct fetches of those sites returned HTTP 403. Where their content shows up here at all, it is relayed through an English-language guide that cites them, or through a search-engine snippet, never a verified direct read.

blocks.title: Glossary
blocks.headExtrasHtml: System names, currencies, and jargon from the Systems guide confirmed
blocks.bodyHtml:
Mastery Skill
Your class's core combat ability, learned automatically at level requirements and raised with Skill Points up to a base cap of 10. expcarry, date unknown1
Specialization
Chosen bonus effects a skill gains at level breakpoints 8, 12, and 16, up to 3 extra effects per skill. Fextralife, date unknown2
Empyrean Trace / Feather
A world collectible turned in at a Monolith for Wisdom Stones. Naming is inconsistent between sources, possibly different translations of the same KR item. Fextralife, date unknown3 Differ, date unknown4
Wisdom Stone
A consumable obtained by exchanging Empyrean Traces/Feathers at a Monolith, grants Skill Points on use. Fextralife, date unknown5
Stigma
An equippable skill-enhancement stone adding build-defining abilities on top of your class kit. First slot unlocks around level 23. expcarry, date unknown6
Stigma Shard
The currency spent to level a Stigma Skill, separate from normal Skill Points. Higher-tier Shards exist for KR levels 21-25. expcarry, date unknown7
Daevanion Board
A permanent node-board progression system, separate from gear, raising combat stats and effective skill levels. First board unlocks at level 12. Fextralife, date unknown8
Daevanion Point
Spent to unlock individual Daevanion board nodes; earned from regional quests, Sealed Dungeons, Strongholds, achievements, and exploration. Overgear, date unknown9
Daevanion Crystal
Earned alongside Daevanion Points from the same sources, also obtainable via material conversion; feeds Daevanion board progression. expcarry, date unknown10
Arcana
A card-based system adding Item Level, combat stats, set bonuses, and effective skill levels at once. Slots include Chalice, Parchment, Compass, Bell, and Mirror, later expanded. expcarry, date unknown11
Training Arcana
A consumable that feeds experience to Arcana cards; tiers are Lesser (200 EXP), Intermediate (600), Superior (1,500), and Ultimate (3,000). expcarry, date unknown12
Mana Stone
A socketed gem added to gear for stats like Crit Rate or Speed, found via dungeons, rewards, or crafting; AION 2's Manastone equivalent. u4n, date unknown13
Soul Codex
Alongside Mana Stones, described as helping gear "scale into late-game without major farming" by increasing attribute effects. Fextralife, date unknown14
Soul Binding
A secondary stat block on gear that reportedly "only grows once you bind it." Single-source, unverified. kodex.yavuz, date unknown15
Theostone
A weapon proc stone, AION 2's Godstone equivalent, socketed into a weapon's dedicated slot for a chance-on-hit effect. One effect per weapon; identical Theostones do not stack. 153 known Theostones cataloged. aion2.online, date unknown16
Enhance Stone
Spent to raise a gear piece's enhancement level. Extraction from a previously-enhanced item refunds 100% of the Enhance Stones spent into it. exitlag, date unknown17
Broker
AION 2's player marketplace/Auction House; Kinah is the only currency usable there. Fextralife, date unknown18
Pantheon
A permanent passive-stat system built from Statues, Colossi, and "Artwork"; placing a Colossus grants points toward a deity domain, each capping at 200 points before converting to flat combat stats. Vortex Gaming, date unknown19
Colossus
A Pantheon item slotted to grant domain points; its rarity (Green/Blue/Purple/Gold) determines bonus strength. rsnxt, date unknown20
Achievement Points
Granted by completing achievements; ties into Daevanion Point/Crystal income. Differ, date unknown21
Title
An earned label from PvP rank, Arena tiers, boss kills, monster-hunting milestones, or events; stat titles grant bonuses like PvP Attack or HP when equipped, some are purely cosmetic. aion2hub, date unknown22
Appearance Collection
A wardrobe-style collection; roughly 700 appearances grants combat speed and cooldown reduction as a milestone bonus. Cash-shop cosmetics do not count toward it. Vortex Gaming, date unknown23
Soul (Pets/Mounts)
A monster drop; farming 10 souls of almost any monster unlocks it as a pet/mount. Also drops from the Shugo Shop and Black Cloud Merchant. Fextralife, date unknown24
Flight Power
A wing's airborne stamina stat, managed via a physics-based "Glide Gauge" rather than a rigid timer. TheGamer, date unknown25
Glide Gauge
The physics-based mechanic underlying Flight Power; running it out mid-air drops you. u4n, date unknown26
Legion
AION 2's guild system, capped at up to 128 members, used for PvE, PvP, crafting, and social access. 6Sword, date unknown27
Legion Hall
Unlocks at Legion level 5, costs 1,000,000 Kinah to rent, houses all five crafting professions' merchants/workbenches together. mmoexp, date unknown28
Legion Coin
Earned for active Legion contribution; spent on Legion-exclusive skins, uniforms, masks, mounts, and wings. u4n, date unknown29
Accuracy
Governs the chance to land an attack; per one source, also affects crit chance. u4n, date unknown30
Precision
A hybrid stat that raises both Accuracy and Crit chance. u4n, date unknown31
PvE Attack / Defense
Comes only from PvE gear; only affects damage dealt to and taken from monsters. exitlag, date unknown32
PvP Attack / Defense
Comes only from PvP gear; only affects damage dealt to and taken from other players. exitlag, date unknown33
Item Level
A gating number for content access, cited around 900-2700+ tiers for Transcendence content. Fextralife, date unknown34
Combat Power ("Atul")
An aggregate power estimate used for matchmaking/ranking-style comparisons. The "Atul" name is single-source and may be a translation artifact. u4n, date unknown35
Transcendence
AION 2's endgame progression/ranking layer, fed by specific dungeons with up to 4 escalating difficulty levels. aion2hub, 2026-0736
Odyle Energy
Spent to open the reward cube after clearing an Expedition or Transcendence dungeon; entry itself is not gated by energy. Normal cube costs 40, Hard costs 60. aion2hub, 2026-0737
Essence Extraction
The gathering skill/action used to mine ore, gather herbs, or cut wood, feeding all five crafting professions. expcarry, date unknown38
Kinah
The main in-game currency; earned from quests, monster kills, dungeons, and vendor sales, spent on repairs, soul-binding, crafting materials, teleports, and gear enhancement, the only currency usable on the Broker. u4n, date unknown39
Quna
The premium/cash-shop currency, obtained mainly via real-money purchase and tradeable for Kinah through a Currency Exchange, spent on cosmetics and Battle Pass premium tiers. u4n, date unknown40
Abyss Points
Earned from daily/weekly PvP-zone quests; presumed to buy Abyss-specific gear/items, not independently confirmed. Fextralife, date unknown41
Centuryroot Token
Spent at a "Shugo Festival" seasonal shop; purpose beyond that event unverified. Fextralife, date unknown42

blocks.title: Glossary Additions
blocks.bodyHtml:
Style Shop
The referenced but unnamed source of post-creation appearance changes; a special currency or cash-shop item is needed to alter your look after character creation finishes, exact item not yet named for global. Fextralife, date unknown1
Rune (accessory)
An accessory-slot item distinct from Manastones, Theostones, and Arcana cards. Named examples: Clash Rune, Devotion Rune. Two good runes are worth roughly 80 item levels. Fextralife, date unknown2 kodex.yavuz, date unknown3
Transfer Crafting
A single-source crafting process that carries a gear piece's enhancement, amplification, and Soul Binding progress into its next-tier upgrade, guaranteed to succeed, resulting item becomes Soul Bound. Unconfirmed by a second source. kodex.yavuz, date unknown4
Legion Hideout
Rentable Legion space, only an officer can rent it, costing 1,000,000 Kinah for 23 days and 15 hours. Distinct from the disputed "Legion Hall" claim in the Legion card on the Systems page. guildmanager.app, date unknown5
Abyss Rank (Trainee through Supreme Commander)
A 20-tier seasonal PvP ranking ladder built on Abyss Points. Ninth-Class Soldier needs 3,000 points; the single Supreme Commander slot needs 25,000,000. KR/TW server data. aion2hub, date unknown6
Pet Genus Insight / Possession Effect
A mechanic where leveling and collecting pets grants passive Combat Power, separate from simply riding a pet as a mount. Vortex Gaming, date unknown7
Odella
A high-tier gathering material (about 6 per gathering session) used to craft "Odella Energy," a Daevanion Crystal-equivalent material, plus higher-tier wings and equipment. Possibly the same underlying resource as this guide's "Odyle Energy," unconfirmed. Vortex Gaming, date unknown8
Inder Boss
A boss encountered while gathering, defeating it is tied to Odella yield. Vortex Gaming, date unknown9
